summary: Thomas Dunn first showed St. Helena's brick tower light in 1873 to mark a Straits shoal; keepers served until 1922, and volunteers run the station now.

lens.note: Original third-and-a-half-order Fresnel lens, shipped from Paris (Pepper); the USLHS record gives the same order. Installed August 1873.

structures.note: 65 feet from foundation to the center of the lens (Pepper)
Joined to the tower by a covered way (Pepper)

access.note: Reached only by boat. Owned and run by the GLLKA, which arranges volunteer stays and visits; the island is a nature preserve held by the Little Traverse Conservancy.

stay.note: Volunteer keeper stays through the GLLKA, mid-June to mid-August, minimum three days, fee covers housing and meals.

events.note: Congress appropriates the money for the light on 10 June 1872 (after the Board asked for it in 1867)
Tower and dwelling built September 1872 to June 1873 (Pepper)
Thomas P. Dunn reports for duty 29 July 1873 (Pepper)
Light first exhibited the evening of 20 September 1873 (Pepper)
New landing crib and boat way; new walks; materials delivered for an oil house (Board report)
Brick oil house with metal door, roof and shelving erected (Board report)
Keeper George E. Leggatt drowned June 1901 (Pepper only; no primary source read)
Keeper Joseph Fountain brings in two men lost on the ice, 7 February 1913
Keeper Fountain and assistant Wallace Hall help repair a disabled motor boat near the station, August 1914
Acetylene lamp with sun valve; keeper Hall transferred 30 June 1922 (Bulletin; Pepper)
Oil to acetylene; fixed to flashing (Board list of changes, 1922)
Great Lakes Lighthouse Keepers Association takes a thirty-year license to the reservation
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP 88000442)
Buildings and reservation transferred to the GLLKA by a bill sponsored by Rep. Bart Stupak, as part of a Coast Guard authorization act (Pepper)
Little Traverse Conservancy buys the island as a nature preserve (Pepper)

corrections.why: Pepper's history and the USLHS place record both give a third-and-a-half-order original lens; the record's events text says order 3.
Pepper gives 65 feet from foundation to the lens center (19.8 m); the record's 21.5 m is not supported by the sources read. The 21.6 m focal height is consistent.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says order 3, Pepper says third-and-a-half, and the USLHS record gives third-and-a-half as its original optic. The story follows third-and-a-half.

notes_for_editor: Sources: Pepper's Seeing the Light history is a community site, so only facts are used, in our own words; its quotations appear only as evidence. The NRHP nomination (88000442) is the 'not yet digitized' placeholder on NPGallery, so the 1988 listing is taken from the GLLKA site. Leggatt's 1901 drowning rests on Pepper alone; newspaper searches for 1901 returned no pages, and loc.gov returned HTTP 520 errors on several tries during this research. Pepper gives the Scouts from 1989 and the GLLKA from 1990; Pepper gives the transfer to GLLKA in 1996, while Wikipedia (not used) gives 1997. Pepper says the Little Traverse Conservancy bought the entire island; GLLKA and the story say the reservation is GLLKA's. The Bulletin's 1913 'lost on the ice' entry and Putnam's blizzard account differ in detail; the story follows the Bulletin for the event and marks Putnam's detail as Putnam's. The Bulletin of 1913 also says 'the light keepers were 72 hours without sleep or rest', but that line refers to the Pilot Island keepers and is not used. The 1915 Commissioner table lists Fountain and Hall under St. Helena; the event it records is not clear, so it is not used. Pepper's spellings differ from the roster (Lousigneau, Legatt, Louis J. Beloungea); roster spellings are used with variants in notes. Fountain's other service (Pepper: South Fox Island and Skillagallee) has no years in the sources, so no other_stations entry is made. The current optic (250 mm, USLHS record) and the light's active status are not quoted from a readable page, so the story does not state them. Range in the record (5.2 nm) is not checked against a Light List. Photos not searched.
